projects.name: MATSim Open Berlin Scenario (v6.x; v5.x lineage)
projects.engine: MATSim (TU Berlin VSP); demand from SrV survey statistical matching (v6) / CEMDAP+CaDyTS (v5)
projects.city_population: Berlin + Brandenburg; v5.2 paper: 'all adult people living in Berlin and Brandenburg' (real population not stated); v6.3 paper: population from Kommunalatlas 2020 (531 zones) + German census; agent count not stated in fetched sources
projects.sample_fraction: 10% (release berlin-v6.3-10pct / v6.4-10pct); 3% and 1% variants also published; v5 was 10%
projects.modes: car, ride (car passenger), public transport, bicycle, walk; commercial/freight traffic added in v6 (long-haul freight + small-scale commercial)
projects.active_modes: v5.2 paper: bicycle and walk teleported (12 km/h, 4 km/h beeline), ride routed on network with car travel time; v6 paper does not state a change
projects.pt_physical: yes - GTFS schedule (VBB), 'simulated based on the actual public transport schedule'; v6 uses GTFS day 2023-06-06
projects.signals: no - v6 paper: 'traffic lights are typically not modeled explicitly'; free speeds calibrated with SUMO microsimulation + routing APIs; v5: OSM inner-city free speeds halved
projects.freight: yes - v5: simplified freight agents from BASt counts; v6: long-haul freight model + small-scale commercial traffic model
projects.fares_pricing: v6: PT priced at 3 EUR/day (761 EUR yearly ticket / 250 days), car 0.149 EUR/km + 5 EUR/day, ride 0.149 EUR/km (Table 1)
projects.validation_rung: survey shares + road link counts (no transit ridership counts)
projects.best_fit: v6.3 (Rakow, Kreuschner, Nagel 2024): mode share MAE < 0.5 percentage points vs SrV for all modes (car 19.93 vs 20.07, ride 5.94/5.96, PT 26.97/26.51, bike 17.81/17.79, walk 29.35/29.68 %); car speeds within routing-API bounds by hour; daily link volumes vs 2018 counts 'generally too low, particularly on motorways' (scatter only, no R2 stated). v5.2 (Ziemke et al. 2019): mode shares car 29.6/30.0 (MiD), PT 22.4/21.0, bike 10.6/11.0, walk 27.5/28.0 %; counts: 8,304 hourly values at 346 stations, mean relative error by hour shown graphically (~20-40 % daytime after mode calibration)
projects.open_source: code GPL-2.0 (v6 repo) ; inputs/outputs CC-BY 4.0
projects.reproducible: yes - v6 pipeline from OSM/GTFS/census/SrV with automated ASC calibration (converges in ~5 runs); v5 from open data + CaDyTS; counts data are the only non-open input
projects.city_agnostic: partly - pipeline described as 'spatially transferable' (v5 paper) and reused for Ruhr; scenario code is Berlin-specific
projects.status: active - repo updated Sep 4 2026; 1,876 commits; v6.4 current; paper Transportation Research Procedia 2025
projects.does_best: Automated mode-share calibration of ASCs driven from survey shares (closed-form update, converges in a handful of runs) plus a three-way check against survey, routing-API speeds and count stations

ours.name: city-digital-twin - Newcastle (NSW) study (this repository)
ours.engine: MATSim end to end, with project-owned Java extensions (src/java/citysim, src/java_signals) for signals, ride pairing and mode-specific constraints
ours.city_population: Newcastle (NSW) region - five LGAs, 1,500 core SA1s, base year 2026
ours.sample_fraction: 25% (standing directive since 1 Sep 2026; the F30 arm the board reads is aborted_20260907T150816_300it_25pct, 25% sample, read at iteration 20)
ours.modes: TWELVE, each scored individually: car, ride, walk, taxi, bike, motorbike, bus, heavy_rail, light_rail, ferry, truck, freight_train
ours.active_modes: physical - walk and bike are simulated on the network, not teleported (positions/walk-and-bike.md)
ours.pt_physical: yes - bus, heavy rail, light rail and ferry run the mapped GTFS schedule on the mapped network; 15 feeds mapped, 0 unmapped stops
ours.signals: yes - SCATS implemented as its published algorithm (registry A.signals.scats.*: target degree of saturation, cycle bounds, ds smoothing/deadband, cycle step) plus transit signal priority (A.signals.tsp.*)
ours.freight: yes - truck as a road vehicle scored on network-wide road-vehicle share; freight rail as timetable-derived level-crossing closures rather than a mobsim vehicle
ours.fares_pricing: yes - Opal fare schedule in the registry (A.fare.*: peak/off-peak by mode, child/senior classes, daily and weekend caps, distance bands) plus priced parking (A.parking.*: charged hours, modes, price percentiles, search time) and a monetary distance rate (C.scoring.monetary_distance_rate)
ours.validation_rung: per-mode ridership, every simulated mode - the top rung, and the only project in this survey attempting it for twelve modes
ours.best_fit: NOT A RESULT. The board's scoreboard is a reading of an ABORTED run (aborted_20260907T150816_300it_25pct) at ITERATION 20, family F30-an-escort-is-priced-as-an-escort, 25% sample. IN CALIBRATION, NO MODE IS INSIDE 10%. car -13.0% and motorbike +15.8% are over 10% but under the stop bar; EIGHT modes are past the 20% stop bar - ride -45.2%, walk +64.7%, taxi +105.6%, bike +198.4%, bus +106.9%, heavy_rail +417.1%, light_rail -30.0%, ferry -63.7%; truck is level-only and freight_train representation-only. This is a CHANGE from the previous pass, which read F28 at its iteration-100 gate with one mode of twelve inside 10% (car +6.6%): the reading has moved back to none, and it is a reading at iteration 20 rather than 100, so the two are not comparable as fits. No run since family F4 has reached its declared horizon, and convergence within 250 iterations is UNMEASURED.
ours.open_source: yes - the repository; OSM-derived layers ODbL 1.0, the rest CC-BY 4.0
ours.reproducible: yes and gated - every derived file regenerable by a committed script from immutable hashed raw downloads, 512 files in data/MANIFEST.csv with hash, rows, producing script, source, licence and retrieval date; everything synthetic seeded (20260810)
ours.city_agnostic: yes by construction - src/, config/schema/, tests/ and run.py must read identically for an unseen city; all 480 registry fields, adapters and geometry live under cities/<city>/, enforced by check_city_agnostic.py and check_hardcoding.py --strict at 0
